key_insight: A three-agent LLM workflow can automatically tune task-specific neural components while keeping the overall model architecture fixed.
engineering_relevance: This offers a transferable, low-touch way to improve specialized scientific ML systems without redesigning the full training pipeline.
method: Analyst identifies the tunable components and experiment objective.
Coder generates code only for those components inside a sandboxed environment.
Recorder logs trials and results to guide iterative refinement.
evidence_signal: Across five tasks, the system improved MNIST accuracy by 13 points, Digits by 6 points, reduced one GNLSE error by about 2491×, cut invariant-preservation error by about 325× in one run and over 100× on average, and reduced KS mass drift by 14×.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable sandbox execution and may be sensitive to prompt quality, task specification, and the narrowness of the allowed code-edit space.
paper_title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
